title: Compiler inventory reports no resolved module closure
commons_coordination: No Commons record filed: MNCS-Commons checkout is on another agent's campaign branch. The owning layer is mncs-language (branch-active, stdlib extraction).
observed_need: mncs-test-verify needs the exact set of modules/files the compiler resolved for a suite, so one obligation's dependency change does not invalidate unrelated obligations in the same repository.
current_language_behavior: `mncs test-inventory` reports the source module's subject identity/fingerprint plus per-test declaration/test-case identities, spans, signatures, effects, and capabilities, but no resolved import closure. mncs-test-verify therefore fingerprints every MNCS source in the repository: docs/scripts changes preserve reuse, but any suite edit conservatively invalidates every obligation in the repo.
why_insufficient: Host-side import resolution would duplicate compiler knowledge (forbidden by the test tool's own architecture). Only the compiler can state authoritatively which files it read.
minimal_reproducer: In a two-suite repository, edit suite A and run mncs-test-verify: obligation B re-executes even though its subject, inventory, and invalidation closure are unchanged, because the shared repository fingerprint covers suite A.
desired_direction: Extend mncs.test-inventory/1 with the resolved module/file closure (content identities); mncs-test-verify will bind per-obligation fingerprints to it and compute affected sets precisely.
workaround: Repository-wide MNCS-source fingerprinting: sound (a superset of what can matter), merely imprecise across obligations.
